newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Nov 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Nov 22.

text.p: The following is a summary of major South Korean political stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not gaurantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666.
- South Korea's banking deregulation is insufficient, and the nation's top priorities are to retrench monetary and fiscal policy and stabilise prices, according to an IMF report.
- President Kim Young-sam, visiting Vietnam on the first leg of this three-nation tour, stressed complementary economic relations between South Korea and Vietnam.
- Korean secondary school students are vulnerable to mental stress arising from extracurricular tutoring.
- President Kim Young-sam supports Vietnam's membership in the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum.
- Korean exports rebound in October after a three-month downturn, with all goods excluding semiconductors showing good performances, according to the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy.

- South Korea is expected to establish diplomatic relations with Cuba sooner or later, vice foreign minister Lee Ki-choo tells parliamentary budget deliberation session yesterday. He also hinted at a possiblity of establishing diplomatic relation with Syria.
